summary: Milestone 2026.09.660 completed 9 experiments, all compute-bound, in 12.0 wall-time minutes. The longest tasks were 'Independently test feedback causality and count-learning conclusions' at 3.25 minutes, 'Bind fourteen complete authorities and ingest the new method limits' at 2.9 minutes, and 'Measure durable count-service cost and preserve all board states' at 2.75 minutes. Sub-phase timing was not recorded within these runs to separate model inference duration from validation scaffolding or artifact serialization overhead.
bottlenecks_identified: 'Independently test feedback causality and count-learning conclusions' was the longest task at 3.25 minutes out of 12.0 total wall-time minutes, but lacks granular sub-phase instrumentation to isolate model inference from verification scaffolding or artifact serialization.

'Bind fourteen complete authorities and ingest the new method limits' (2.9 minutes) and 'Measure durable count-service cost and preserve all board states' (2.75 minutes) accounted for an additional 5.65 minutes combined without recorded intra-task phase durations.

The top three compute-bound tasks accounted for 8.9 out of 12.0 total wall-time minutes (approx. 74% of milestone execution time), with timing reconstructed from disk mtimes rather than continuous runtime stage logs.

The GPU monitor report provides an isolated post-completion snapshot (PID 772157 on GPU 0 with 18054MB allocated at 0% utilization, GPU 1 idle at 4MB) after milestone execution, leaving GPU utilization across active compute execution windows unmeasured.
Task launch records did not log model concurrency or runner dispatch details, although all completed tasks were single-model runs where DualGPURunner multi-model dispatch is not applicable.
improvements_suggested: Instrument granular sub-phase duration timers and monotonic stage logging inside feedback causality, authority binding, and count-service workflows to isolate model inference latency from validation scaffolding and disk serialization.

Deploy continuous, task-aligned accelerator telemetry during compute-bound executions to sample live GPU utilization and VRAM occupancy across active compute windows rather than relying on point-in-time monitor snapshots.
Record explicit model concurrency and runner dispatch metadata in experiment task receipts to audit DualGPURunner eligibility whenever two or more models run concurrently.
Implement runtime milestone-scoped execution logging to avoid reliance on post-hoc disk-mtime timing reconstruction.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Instrument sub-phase duration timers and per-stage progress logging inside the feedback causality audit and authority binding pipelines.
Deploy continuous accelerator telemetry during compute-bound task execution to record live GPU utilization and VRAM occupancy across active execution windows.
Emit explicit model concurrency and runner dispatch metadata in experiment receipts to audit DualGPURunner engagement on multi-model workloads.
meta_reflection: The milestone completed 9 compute-bound tasks in 12.0 wall-time minutes, with execution concentrated in feedback causality testing (3.25 minutes), authority binding (2.9 minutes), and count-service cost measurement (2.75 minutes). The post-run GPU monitor report confirms an idle llama.cpp process on GPU 0 after completion but cannot evaluate active-window compute efficiency, and because only single-model tasks were executed, no DualGPURunner multi-model dispatch opportunity was missed. Sub-phase timing and continuous execution telemetry are necessary next steps to identify actionable latency optimizations.
